name: Eswatini

findings.controller: US Department of State (Clean Network programme)
findings.local_actor: Ministry of Information, Communications and Technology
findings.summary: Eswatini and the US issued a joint statement making Eswatini the first African country in the US Clean Network programme, committing to a common approach to 5G network security aimed at excluding Huawei-type vendors.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 1: non-binding joint statement, no procurement or exclusion order. still_current false because SWZ-002 withdrew it within days. OSIRIS republishes Ecofin, so independence from Digital Watch is partial; both trace to the same joint statement. Ecofin page failed to load.

findings.controller: US Department of State (Clean Network programme)
findings.local_actor: Ministry of Information, Communications and Technology
findings.summary: Days after joining, the ICT ministry withdrew the Clean Network joint statement, citing legitimacy problems with its approval process and saying development should weigh equally with security; Huawei said it had received no notice.
findings.analyst_inference: Reversal of a US-pole Tier 1 commitment. Stated reason is procedural (approval legitimacy); coded geopolitical on the ministry's own security-versus-development framing and timing after the US transition, which is inference and a reviewer call (regulatory is the alternative). Not reconfirmed for 2026.

findings.summary: A profile of MTN Eswatini reports a 2016 network revamp with Huawei, around the operator's July 2016 LTE launch on 1800 MHz.
findings.analyst_inference: Single opened general-press profile, one line on Huawei with no contract detail; whether RAN, core or both is not stated. Tier 5 assumes the revamp was completed and operated. Pre-2020 and not reconfirmed as current, so the map should halve it. Needs an S1/S2 source.

findings.controller: Google (with Stardust Inc and SHE Powers Africa, UAE)
findings.summary: On the UNGA sidelines, Eswatini's ICT minister signed an MOU with Google, Stardust Inc and UAE-based SHE Powers Africa to build skills in AI and cybersecurity and improve government services; no model, platform or value named.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole us on Google as the only named technology provider; Stardust's nationality not verified and the UAE party is a women's organisation. Skills/innovation MOU, not model adoption, so it may belong outside the models layer. Single opened local source.
